definition: A single entry point in front of many APIs that handles the concerns every API shares - authentication, keys, rate limits, versioning, transformation, caching, analytics - so each API only implements its business logic. It becomes critical infrastructure, so it needs an SLA and redundancy.
example: Every partner call to the shop's orders, catalogue and stock APIs passes through one API gateway that applies the partner's limits.

definition: Azure's API gateway service: a gateway every call passes through, a management plane for APIs, products and policies, and a developer portal for consumers. Tiers run from pay-per-call Consumption to Premium; Developer has no SLA and is not for production.
example: apim-shop-prod on Standard v2 fronts the orders, catalogue and warehouse APIs behind Front Door.

definition: An XML pipeline in API Management that runs on each call - inbound, backend, outbound and on-error - at global, product, API or operation scope. Policies validate tokens, apply rate limits and quotas, cache, rewrite URLs and headers, and authenticate to backends with a managed identity. Business logic belongs in the API, not in policies.
example: The Partners product policy validates an Entra token and allows ten calls a second per subscription.

definition: A package in API Management that consumers subscribe to: one or more APIs plus the rules for using them, such as rate limits, quotas, whether a key or token is required, and whether sign-up needs approval.
example: The Marketplace product exposes the catalogue and stock APIs at five calls a second, with approval required.

definition: The key a consumer receives when subscribing to an API Management product, sent on each call to identify them for limits and analytics. It is a shared string, not proof of identity, so pair it with a validated token for anything sensitive, rotate it, and never ship it in a mobile app.
example: Each delivery partner has its own subscription key, so the weekend's runaway script is identified and throttled immediately.

definition: Capping how many calls a consumer may make in a short window, often with a longer-period quota as well. Calls over the limit get 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header and never reach the backend, so one consumer cannot starve the others.
example: A partner limited to ten calls a second gets 429s at the eleventh, and checkout is unaffected.

definition: The self-service website API Management generates for API consumers: documentation from each API's OpenAPI description, a console to try calls, product sign-up and key management. It replaces documents emailed to partners.
example: The marketplace team signs up in the developer portal, reads the catalogue API docs and receives a key once approved.

definition: The standard format for describing an HTTP API - its operations, parameters, request and response shapes and security - in JSON or YAML. Tools generate documentation, clients and tests from it, and API Management imports it to define an API.
example: The Node API generates its OpenAPI file at build time, and the pipeline imports it into API Management on every release.
